insights: Tech breakthroughs and robotics consistently hit 1,000+ views on Shorts (Tesla Roadster 1,308, Quantinuum 1,305, Aging 1,126, Unitree 1,111), while general science/nature questions saw lower traction (Icebergs 543, Submarines 49).
Subscriber conversions come almost entirely from 'Future scenario' and high-tech breakthrough Shorts (Quantinuum +4, Tesla Roadster +4, Aging +3), whereas explainers and teasers gained 0 subscribers.
Telling viewers to check the channel kills Short retention: mentioning 'The full breakdown is on our channel' triggered an immediate 23.6% drop-off at 38.6s.
Opening hooks between 4s and 7s lose 4% to 10% of viewers when stating background setup instead of delivering fast curiosity triggers (e.g., Icebergs dropped 9.8% at 6.9s).
Call-to-actions are failing across the board: 10 out of 12 videos got 0 comments, indicating ending questions need to be controversial or directly debatable rather than rhetorical.
'News' format Shorts paired with countdown or future styles achieve the best retention, consistently averaging 63% to 68% view duration.

Long-form data is too thin to confirm reach patterns (only 3 videos), but specific numerical titles ('at 2,000°C' with 468 views) vastly outperformed vague conceptual titles ('The Engineering Secret' with 4 views).
